title: surge-window-scheduler-and-sla-mapping-q3-2026
summary: Operational playbook for scheduling planned surge windows across NA / EU / APAC in Q3 2026, mapping those windows to SLO tiers and defining buffer targets, on-call provisioning responsibilities, and automated triggers. This doc is intentionally tactical: short notice surge windows, emergency buffer allocation, and SLA mapping for new Dedicated onboarding windows.
assumptions: 1) Baseline fleet = current committed reserved GPUs per region (see infra billing export, May 2026). 2) Typical 24h rolling utilization during PLG peaks: NA 68%, EU 62%, APAC 55%. 3) New Dedicated customer trials increase tail load by +12–30% in onboarding week. 4) Cold-start boot time for additional nodes: 6–12 minutes depending on cloud provider. 5) Automated autoscaler can add up to 40% burst within region if quota available.

Week of 2026-07-05: Wave Amber (low-friction bursts) — enable 20% autoscaler burst in NA and EU following canary traffic; Ops lead: Ethan.
Week of 2026-07-19: Wave Jade (customer onboarding window) — allocate pre-warmed pool: NA +40 GPUs, EU +20 GPUs, retention 72h; Testing: load test 120% of expected tail.
2026-08-02 to 2026-08-16: Wave Topaz (marketing spike support) — reserve planned slack: NA +60 GPUs from cloud credits, APAC +30 GPUs; Scale policy: immediate fallback to compatible quantized variant if latency > 450ms P95.
2026-09-06: Contingency window for Enterprise rollouts — pre-approved cross-region spill to secondary zone if NA saturation > 92% for 15 consecutive minutes.
slo_mapping:
Tier 1 (Enterprise, SLA): P95 < 200ms generation for short chats (<256 tokens), target buffer = 30% spare GPUs in-region.
Tier 2 (Dedicated web scale): P95 < 350ms, buffer = 20%.
Tier 3 (Hosted API public): P95 < 450ms, buffer = 10%, degrade via quantized fallback and batching.
Compliance: For any Tier 1 customer rolling over 72h, notify legal + account manager; record decisions in incident channel.
trigger_playbook:
1) Monitoring trigger: region GPU utilization > 85% sustained for 10m => automated pre-warm of standby pool (if quotas allow) and page oncall-sre.
2) Alert trigger: P95 > SLA threshold for two consecutive 5m windows => initiate immediate model-variant fallback and increase worker concurrency limits; page infra-ops.
3) Quota exhaustion: if cloud quota prevents hot add, trigger cross-region spill policy and open emergency capacity request to cloud team.
4) Manual escalate: product ops can request temporary PRD uplift for prioritized customers; require exec approval for costs > $25k/day.
runbook_actions: Assign surge owner for each wave (default: Ethan for NA, Mariana for EU, Liam for APAC)
Schedule dry-run 72h before each wave (loadgen + smoke tests)
Pre-authorize cloud cross-region burst for contingency windows
Tag affected routes in Redwood Console for focused tracing
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: concurrent enterprise rollouts + marketing spike overload. Mitigation: stagger onboarding windows by at least 7 days; enforce pre-warm gating.
Risk: cloud quota delays. Mitigation: submit quota increase requests 14 days prior and maintain small committed buffer in each region.
Risk: cost overrun from bursts. Mitigation: track per-route token burn daily and suspend non-essential batch jobs during surge window.
open_questions: Do we want a hard cap on per-customer burst (suggested: 25% of region reserved) ?
Confirm billing owner for cross-region emergency bursts (product finance contact needed)
Should we pre-warm quantized variants by default for Tier 3 during spikes?
